A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CASteer. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison. Retained content can be matched despite expanded appendices and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original CASteer experiments on inappropriate-content removal, object erasure, image quality and editing, together with user studies in Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results and user studies and adds artist-style evaluations, ablations, paired-concept erasure and transfer experiments.

M1.justification: v2 describes averaging concept vectors or applying them successively. v4 introduces Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization before successive multi-concept steering in Section 3.4 and Appendix M. This is a limited procedural extension; single-concept vector construction, adaptive weighting, clipping and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 adds artist-style erasure and preservation evaluations for famous and modern artist groups, plus qualitative mosaic/origami erasure. Appendix K adds an implicit actor-identity erasure case. Appendix M evaluates Snoopy with nudity or Mickey simultaneously, extending coverage beyond v2's combined inappropriate-content task. The earlier style-transfer experiments are retained and are distinct from these new erasure tasks.

E2.justification: DoCo (Wu et al., 2025) is newly evaluated in the nudity comparison (Table 1), concrete-object comparison (Figure 4 and Table 36), and implicit-prompt comparisons (Figure 3 and Appendix K). Existing comparators, including SPM, SAFREE, ESD and Receler, remain.

E3.justification: v4 introduces artist-style evaluation using LPIPS and GPT-4o judgments, together with constant-weight controls, last-36-layer tests, SD-1.5 transfer with 50 denoising steps, and first-step-only vector reuse. For the retained prompt-count ablation, preservation changes from Mickey-only FID in v2 Appendix G.1 to average FID over other concepts in v4 Appendix H.1. These additions and the reported metric revision substantially expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v4 adds spatial dot-product heatmaps and a constant-versus-adaptive weighting ablation. It replaces v2's Snoopy steering-strength plot with broader nudity and image-quality sensitivity tables across three models, extends partial-layer analysis to styles versus objects, and adds checkpoint-transfer and single-step-vector analyses in Appendices N–O. Existing layer-choice, steering-vector visualization and UMAP analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 already evaluates three disjoint prompt sets and displays individual outcomes and their mean. v4 Appendix H.1 additionally specifies different random seeds, and Figure 29 reports mean plus/minus standard deviation. Appendix E reports GPT-4o judgment accuracy averaged over three runs. No increase in the retained ablation's three-run count is stated.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive style-erasure, weighting, sensitivity, paired-concept and transfer results. Among retained settings, Table 3 changes clipped SD-1.4 CLIP-30K from 30.09 to 31.09, and unclipped SANA nudity detections change from 11 to 9 (v2 Table 12; v4 Table 14). However, v4 Table 20 still reports 30.09, leaving that value unresolved. Transfer and first-step-only results concern new experimental conditions.

T1.justification: v4 adds Appendix L's local Jacobian formulation, bounded perturbation sets, a theorem proving inclusion of embedding-reachable perturbations within direct CA perturbations, a rank condition for equality, and an optimal-loss corollary with proofs. v2 has steering equations but no corresponding formal comparison. v4 also inserts the missing beta factor into Equation 5 and adds a Householder norm-preservation rationale.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: training-free selective erasure of concrete and abstract concepts, multiple simultaneous erasures, broad backbone applicability and state-of-the-art performance. The added evidence does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations for why strong unclipped steering can reintroduce nudity, why late-layer steering can suit styles better than concrete objects, and why simple averaging may fail for semantically unrelated concepts. Appendix L qualifies its expressivity argument through a local, idealized formulation. These substantially expand mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries; Appendix A's original limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 supplies a repository link in the abstract, supplementing v2's pseudocode and described code ZIP. It documents the GPT-4o judgment prompt, SPM/DoCo checkpoint provenance, and the 50-step alignment used for SD-1.4-to-SD-1.5 transfer. Existing prompt templates, pseudocode, V100 hardware information and SDXL/SANA timing details are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to Wu et al. (2025) for DoCo and Zhang et al. (2018) for LPIPS. The new theoretical appendix further motivates intervention in CA outputs relative to prompt embeddings, while the related-work section and overall research positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, conclusion and most retained appendix prose preserve their wording and order. v4 makes local language and cross-reference edits, expands selected explanations, and adds a style-erasure discussion and appendix sections. The revision mainly appends scientific material rather than extensively rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adds heatmaps, style-erasure panels and substantial new tables. It redraws the Snoopy comparison, including its FID-axis orientation, adds uncertainty bars to the prompt-count plot, and expands Mickey comparisons with DoCo rows. v2's steering-strength plot and two COCO example grids are removed. Many other figures are retained and renumbered; v4 Figures 49–50 duplicate the same comparison panel.

improvement.justification: The new weighting controls and heterogeneous-pair tests address gaps in v2's support for its adaptive and multi-concept claims. Expanded style evaluation, variability reporting and the local theoretical argument also strengthen the paper. The net gain is limited by reporting defects in the additions: Appendix E reverses the LPIPS directions shown in the tables, Tables 3 and 20 disagree on clipped CLIP-30K, and Table 34 leaves FID values blank. These issues reduce confidence in parts of the expanded evidence.
